newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper may re-test $2,390 resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper may re-test $2,390 resistance.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices may build on Tuesday's fairly bullish close and a re-test of resistance at $2,390 is possible, analysts said on Wednesday.
For aluminium, though, the increasingly heavy overbought position might lead to consolidation, they said.
COPPER
After the distractions of zinc's white knuckle ride on Tuesday, copper could be ready for another upside move.
The London close ($2,360/$2,365) above Monday's level had encouraged the bulls, who forecast tests at $2,390 and, if passed, $2,400, analysts said.
However, other analysts said copper had to close above $2,386 before the uptrend could be backed with confidence.
Technically there were hints of copper moving into a range defined by support at the 10-day moving average of $2,313 and resistance at the declining 30-day figure of $2,373.
Copper was essentially consolidating, but the short-term trend was higher, involving a re-test of $2,400, analysts said.
"The longer term outlook looks bearish with stocks increasing and expanding supply hitting the market," said Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff and Co.
At 0750 GMT copper was indicated at $2,360/$2,365, unchanged from London's late Tuesday level.
ALUMINIUM
The relative strength index rose again yesterday to 76, suggesting overbought aluminium was due for a correction, analysts said.
That made for indecisiveness at the highs despite a positive close on Tuesday.
Although consolidation was likely, there was a chance of testing $1,707 and $1,712 resistances, which would signpost targets at $1,725 and $1,750, they said.
"While we feel aluminium still has a long way to go on the upside, it is currently beginning to enter overbought territory and could therefore see a corrective pullback emerge," said Squires.
If so, the support levels could be at $1,665 then $1,650, be said.
At 0800 GMT, aluminium was indicated at $1,702/$1,704, two dollars above the late London level.
